title: Threads of blue
caption: The Seyfert galaxy IC 4870, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: IC 4870 · constellation Pavo · about 28 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Bright blue threads ripple through IC 4870 like a misshapen system of lakes. In front of it, nearby stars gleam with diffraction spikes, and a few other galaxies hide among them, looking like stars until you look closely. DeLisle Stewart discovered IC 4870 in 1900, and it lies approximately 28 million light-years away.

The galaxy has an active galactic nucleus, or AGN, a central region so luminous that it can be brighter than all the rest of the galaxy put together. AGNs give off radiation across the whole spectrum, from radio waves to gamma rays, powered by a central supermassive black hole consuming material that strays too close. IC 4870 is a Seyfert galaxy, a kind of AGN with characteristic emission lines.

Hubble has imaged it for several studies of nearby active galaxies. Small-scale structure can reveal traces of collisions and mergers, central bars, nuclear starbursts, jets and outflows, and other links between a nucleus and its surroundings.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.09 x 1.78 arcminutes) and distance (28 million light years), the frame spans roughly 25,000 × 14,000 light-years. Its light set out about 28 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys observed IC 4870 in visible light at 606 nm and 814 nm. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Hubble's sharp view resolves small structures near the galaxy's nucleus, and its exposures gather far more light than an eye can.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

alt: A galaxy streaked with bright blue threads, surrounded by foreground stars with spikes and a few small background galaxies.
